issues.legal_issue: A revenue court’s eviction decree does not bar a later civil title suit by res judicata when the dispute over whether the occupant is a tenant or holds a different status was outside the revenue court’s jurisdiction.
material_facts: The landlords sought the occupant’s eviction in a revenue court on the ground that he had defaulted in paying rent, and the court decreed eviction.
The occupant was evicted and did not appeal the revenue court’s decree.
In a later civil suit, the occupant claimed to be a mortgagee in possession rather than a tenant and sought restoration of possession, challenging the revenue court’s jurisdiction.
The revenue court could hear an eviction suit between landlord and tenant but could not determine the disputed relationship or whether the occupant was a tenant or a mortgagee.
issues.conclusion: The revenue court’s decree did not operate as res judicata, so the subsequent civil suit asserting title was not barred.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 77(3) of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, the revenue court’s jurisdiction over a landlord’s suit to eject a tenant presupposes the landlord-tenant relationship; it does not extend to deciding a serious dispute about whether that relationship exists. The key test for res judicata under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, or analogous principles is whether the first court could decide the issue raised in the later suit. If it could not, its decision does not bar that later suit. Civil-court jurisdiction is not readily treated as excluded. The Court relied on Raj Lakshmi Dasi v. Banamali Sen, Om Prakash Gupta v. Rattan Singh, Shri Raja Durga Singh of Solan v. Tholu, Magiti Sasamal v. Pandab Bissoi, Lal Chand v. Radha Kishan, and State of Tamil Nadu v. Ramalinga Samigal Madam, and referred to Secretary of State v. Mask and Company and Dhulabhai v. State of Madhya Pradesh.

rule.if: subsequent_civil_title_suit and prior_revenue_eviction_decree and landlord_tenant_relationship_disputed and first_court_could_not_determine_relationship

predicates.subsequent_civil_title_suit: After an eviction proceeding, the occupant brought a civil suit asserting a title or status inconsistent with being a tenant.
predicates.prior_revenue_eviction_decree: A revenue court had previously decreed the landlord’s request to evict the occupant as a tenant.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_disputed: The occupant disputed that the relationship between the parties was that of landlord and tenant.
predicates.first_court_could_not_determine_relation: The revenue court hearing the eviction proceeding lacked jurisdiction to decide whether the occupant was a tenant or held a different status.

issues.definition: When an occupant brings a civil title suit after a revenue-court eviction decree, disputes the asserted landlord-tenant relationship, and the first court could not determine that relationship, the later suit is not barred by res judicata.
